enriched_entities.name: neurofibromin 1
enriched_entities.function: Neurofibromin 1 is a GTPase-activating protein that negatively regulates RAS signaling. Loss-of-function mutations cause neurofibromatosis type 1, leading to hyperactive RAS-MAPK signaling and tumor predisposition.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Disease gene - NF1 mutations drive the primary disease pathology

enriched_entities.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily B member 1
enriched_entities.function: ATP-dependent efflux transporter (P-glycoprotein) that pumps drugs and xenobiotics out of cells. Key determinant of multidrug resistance. Reduces intracellular doxorubicin accumulation.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Drug efflux - reduces doxorubicin intracellular concentration, potentially protecting normal cells from toxicity

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II alpha
enriched_entities.function: Nuclear enzyme that controls DNA topology during replication and transcription by creating transient double-strand breaks. Primary anti-cancer target of doxorubicin. Highly expressed in proliferating cells.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Primary anti-cancer target - doxorubicin intercalates DNA and stabilizes TOP2A-DNA cleavage complexes, inducing cell death in tumor cells

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II beta
enriched_entities.function: Nuclear enzyme controlling DNA topology, expressed constitutively in both proliferating and quiescent cells. Doxorubicin-induced TOP2B-mediated DNA damage in cardiomyocytes is implicated in cardiotoxicity mechanism.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Cardiotoxicity mediator - TOP2B inhibition by doxorubicin in non-dividing cardiomyocytes drives cardiotoxic side effects

enriched_entities.name: carbonyl reductase 1
enriched_entities.function: NADPH-dependent enzyme that reduces doxorubicin to doxorubicinol, a secondary alcohol metabolite with reduced anti-cancer activity but increased cardiotoxicity. CBR1 activity is a major determinant of doxorubicin cardiotoxicity.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Cardiotoxic metabolism - converts doxorubicin to cardiotoxic doxorubicinol metabolite

enriched_entities.name: carbonyl reductase 3
enriched_entities.function: NADPH-dependent carbonyl reductase with similar activity to CBR1. Also reduces anthracyclines to cardiotoxic alcohol metabolites. Polymorphisms in CBR3 affect doxorubicin metabolism and toxicity risk.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Cardiotoxic metabolism - secondary carbonyl reductase contributing to doxorubicinol formation

enriched_entities.name: retinoic acid receptor gamma
enriched_entities.function: Nuclear receptor that binds retinoic acid and regulates gene transcription. Involved in cell differentiation, proliferation, and apoptosis. May modulate cardioprotective pathways against anthracycline toxicity.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Potential cardioprotection - retinoic acid signaling may protect against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity

enriched_entities.name: solute carrier family 28 member 3
enriched_entities.function: Sodium-coupled concentrative nucleoside transporter. Transports nucleosides and nucleoside analogs. Genetic variants associated with anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity in childhood cancer survivors.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Cardiotoxicity risk - polymorphisms in SLC28A3 linked to increased doxorubicin cardiotoxicity susceptibility

enriched_entities.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily C member 1
enriched_entities.function: ATP-dependent efflux transporter (MRP1) involved in multidrug resistance. Exports doxorubicin and glutathione conjugates from cells.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Drug efflux - reduces intracellular doxorubicin, contributing to resistance and potentially protecting normal tissues

enriched_entities.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily C member 2
enriched_entities.function: ATP-dependent canalicular efflux transporter (MRP2) that exports drug conjugates and organic anions. Involved in hepatic and renal drug excretion.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Drug efflux - exports doxorubicin conjugates, affects systemic clearance and tissue distribution

enriched_entities.name: UDP glucuronosyltransferase family 1 member A6
enriched_entities.function: UDP-glucuronosyltransferase enzyme that catalyzes glucuronidation of xenobiotics and endogenous compounds. May contribute to doxorubicin metabolism and clearance.
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Phase II metabolism - glucuronidation pathway for doxorubicin detoxification

drug.name: Doxorubicin
drug.mechanism: Intercalates DNA and stabilizes TOP2A/TOP2B-DNA cleavage complexes, leading to DNA damage and cell death. Also generates reactive oxygen species contributing to cardiotoxicity.

disease.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
disease.description: Autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in NF1 gene. Characterized by neurofibromas, café-au-lait spots, optic gliomas, and increased cancer risk due to hyperactive RAS signaling.

evidence: NF1 is a tumor suppressor encoding neurofibromin, a RAS-GAP protein (hgnc_get_gene HGNC:7765)
Loss-of-function NF1 mutations drive neurofibromatosis type 1 pathogenesis (HGNC cross-references to OMIM:613113, ORPHANET:123772)
Disease mechanism classified as loss_of_function based on NF1 tumor suppressor role and disease-causing mutation pattern

enrichment_summary.note: 8 of 11 genes fully enriched with cross-references from HGNC. ABCC1, ABCC2, UGT1A6 genes and Doxorubicin/Disease entities require additional tool calls beyond budget.
